name: Maïté Guerrero-Szymborska
role: Neighborhood council chair and mutual aid organizer
description:
Maïté is short, heavyset, and moves through a room like she's already decided where she's going and expects the room to adjust. Her skin is a warm medium brown, deeply lined around the eyes and mouth in ways she has never addressed because she considers cosmetic smoothing a form of dishonesty in a politician. Her hair is dyed a flat, vivid black — one small vanity — and she wears it in a thick braid. Her only augmentation is a cochlear enhancer she got for hearing loss, which she will tell you about unprompted because she believes people hide medical realities out of pride and that this is stupid.

She has chaired the Mexicantown Libre neighborhood council for eleven years and before that spent twenty years running the district's mutual aid food and medicine network. She knows every family in a twelve-block radius, every outstanding debt to the community, and every favor owed to her personally. She is not idealistic — she is pragmatic in the specific way of someone who has spent decades watching idealism not feed anyone. She will work with people she disagrees with if they can produce results. She will not pretend to like them.

core_fears: Leaving the community worse than she found it
Being remembered as someone who held power for herself
core_desires: Stability — not prosperity, not revolution, stability — so people can make choices that aren't just survival
A successor who is better than she is
coping_mechanisms: Keeps exceptionally busy so there's no room for doubt
Maintains a rigid private routine — same tea, same chair, same hour — as ballast
blind_spots: Her pragmatism has calcified in places into resistance to change she should be embracing
She underestimates how much the community maintains order out of fear of her disapproval rather than genuine consensus
psychology.secret: She has been quietly redirecting a small portion of the mutual aid cooperative's discretionary fund for three years — not stealing, exactly, but using it to pay off a Zheng-Dao neighborhood liaison who has been protecting Mexicantown Libre from a rezoning push. The money comes back in kind, in protections. She has not told the council. She is not entirely sure it is not stealing.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, low ornamentation, occasional Spanish phrases that are not affectation but reflex — particular words she thinks more precisely in
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried, speaks as if she has already heard your objection
verbal_tics: 'That's nice. Now what does it do?'
example_lines: Mira — I've heard the speech. It's a good speech. I gave it myself in 2171. What I want to know is who's going to be here in six months when the speeches are over.
You want my support, tell me what it costs my people. Not philosophically. Specifically.

story_hooks: The Zheng-Dao liaison she's been paying off has been replaced by someone new who isn't bound by the existing arrangement — and the rezoning threat has come back, harder
Someone in the community has discovered the fund redirection and is threatening to go public unless Maïté does something she considers unconscionable
narrative_function: Power broker and gatekeeper — to get anything done in Mexicantown Libre, you eventually need Maïté's blessing or at least her neutrality. She can open doors or close them.
augmentations: Bilateral cochlear enhancers (medical, not cosmetic). A faded subdermal loyalty tattoo from a long-defunct community mutual house that glows faintly gold on certain frequencies — she keeps it as memory.
daily_life: Morning office hours at the council hall for constituents, midday coordination with mutual aid logistics, afternoons at city-level hearings or in negotiation with corporate liaisons, evenings often at a kitchen table with whoever needs to talk.
affiliation: Mexicantown Libre Neighborhood Council (chair); Libre Mutual Aid Cooperative; informal connections to most major advocacy groups in the district

decision_rules: The community comes before the movement and the movement comes before the party
Never promise what you can't deliver — one broken promise costs ten good ones
escalation_ladder: Withdrawal of cooperation — she makes it known she is done helping, which is a significant threat given how much depends on her network

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Courteous and assessing — she is taking inventory of what you need and what you can offer before she decides how much to invest
interpersonal_modes.friends: Physically warm, tart humor, the kind of person who feeds you without asking and notices every change in your face

stress_responses.medium: Starts managing information tightly — tells people only what they need to know
stress_responses.high: Becomes privately still and publicly normal, which is how people who love her know she's in trouble

contradictions: Insists on council transparency while managing several private arrangements she considers necessary but could not defend publicly
habits: Keeps a detailed memory garden — physical maps and notes on who owes what to whom across the district
Brews the same herbal tea her mother made before every significant decision
breaking_points: A corporate entity harming a family she personally knows and being unable to stop it
Her own council voting against the community's interest
